title: Which digit tells us that ten divides a number?
description: The number eight thousand five hundred and sixty is broken into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Counting the tens shows that nothing is left over, and Keeko's doubt, that the tens digit decides, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number with zero in the ones place is made only of tens, so ten divides it exactly. Watch for students who look at the tens digit instead of the ones digit.

source: Is 8560 divisible by 10? Do you agree that numbers divisible by 10 are those that end with 0?
video_script.why: The child sees that a zero in the ones place leaves no single ones, so the number is a whole number of tens.
video_script.substitution: Split the number by place value and count the tens, then read the ones place.
video_script.anchor: the number 8560 split into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones
video_script.wrong_answer: not divisible by ten, because its tens digit is six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the number is not divisible by ten because its tens digit is six. The ones place is the one that matters, and it holds zero, so the six tens are a whole number of tens and the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, eight thousand five hundred and sixty is divisible by ten

final_answer.value: Yes, 8560 is divisible by 10; a number is divisible by 10 exactly when it ends in 0
final_answer.spoken: yes, eight thousand five hundred and sixty is divisible by ten, and a number is divisible by ten exactly when it ends in zero

maths_rules: a number of tens has no single ones, so it ends in 0; a number that ends in 0 has no single ones, so it is a number of tens
so a number is divisible by 10 exactly when it ends in 0
video_script.design: One idea: zero in the ones place means only tens are present. Assumes place value. Wrong idea: the tens digit decides. The place value chart stays on the board to the end.
